SSGC's own OGRA regulatory filing 'Declaration of Capacity of the Gas Transmission Pipeline System - SSGC' (Format Schedule-II of TPA Rule 2018) lists a distinct 'ILBP Region' (Indus Left Bank Pipeline) entry point at Nawabshah, separate from the Sukkur/Hyderabad/IRBP/Karachi regions, feeding a corridor that runs south toward the Karachi region exit points (Nawabshah, Tando Adam, Thatta, Dhabeji listed as ILBP-region exit points in the same document) - this is SSGC's own transmission-system regulatory disclosure, not a GEM citation. Separately, Business Recorder ('Interview with Iqbal Z Ahmed: SSGC clarification') independently confirms 'Indus Left Bank Pipeline (ILBP) system' as a real, named SSGC transmission asset in an official SSGC statement responding to a JJVL dispute (unrelated to GEM, unrelated to this line's specs) - this is the one source that cleanly passed url_verifier.py. Two independent, non-GEM sources therefore corroborate that a real ILBP transmission corridor exists running from Nawabshah toward Karachi and is owned/operated by SSGC, i.e. existence is not a hallucination/GEM-only artifact. CLASSIFICATION: correct - the OGRA document is explicitly a 'Transmission System' capacity declaration under Pakistan's Third Party Access rules, so 'transmission' (not gathering/distribution) is the right PipelineType. ATTRIBUTION: Owner = Sui Southern Gas Co (SSGC) 100% is confirmed - SSGC self-identifies as 'the Transporter' on the same OGRA filing and the ILBP corridor sits squarely in SSGC's Sindh franchise territory (not SNGPL's Punjab/KP territory). Location (Nawabshah, Sindh -> Karachi, Sindh) matches the ILBP region geography in the OGRA filing. CAVEAT / what I could NOT independently pin down: neither source names a segment called exactly 'Nawabshah-Karachi Gas Pipeline', nor states its length (290 km), diameter (16 in), or capacity (80 MMcf/d) as a single-segment figure - the OGRA filing's ILBP entry-point figure (668 MMCFD, per the January 2020 and March 2021 filings) is the AGGREGATE capacity of the whole multi-loop ILBP corridor at Nawabshah, not a single 80 MMcf/d line, so it neither confirms nor contradicts GEM's 80 MMcf/d - it is plausible GEM's row represents one loop/segment within that larger corridor (the roster shows GEM tracks several other loops/segments along shared corridors under separate PIDs, e.g. Sui-Multan Loopline I/II/III, Qadirpur Gas Pipeline/Loopline/(LNG Phase II)), but I found no source that isolates this specific 80 MMcf/d, 16-inch, 290 km segment by that name. A LinkedIn engineer profile mentions maintenance work on 'the 16" Indus Left Bank Pipeline' at marker points MP-315/321/323, which is directionally consistent with a 16-inch ILBP segment, but a personal LinkedIn profile is not an independently verifiable/citable source so I did not use it. Also checked and ruled out a false lead: SSGC news coverage of being 'asked to build LNG pipeline From Karachi to Nawabshah' (ssgc.com.pk/web/?p=5317, 2017) is about an entirely DIFFERENT, much larger proposed Russia-financed North-South/Pakistan Stream LNG megaproject (Karachi-Lahore, 42-56in class) - not this pipeline and not a duplicate of it. Nawabshah ... Name of the Transporter: Sui Southern Gas Company' via `pdftotext -layout` - but url_verifier.py's raw-HTTP substring check cannot extract text from this binary PDF and reports a FAIL ('200 but missing expected'), a known false-negative class per the verifier's own docstring (PDF text isn't reachable via r.text). resolutions.recommendation: Existence, ownership, status, and the length/diameter numbers are all solidly confirmed -- but P4107 is likely mis-structured as a single row. SNGPL's own transmission-segment inventory (Annual Reports 2015-2018, unchanged across 4 consecutive years) lists 'SIDHNAI - FAISALABAD' as FOUR separate table rows by diameter: 18-in/163.58km, 24-in/50.24km, 30-in/53.29km, 36-in/26.42km. GEM split the 18-in line off as its own row (P4106, exact match), then combined the remaining three (24/30/36-in) into ONE row (P4107) with a summed length (50.24+53.29+26.42=129.95km, exact match to GEM's LengthKnown) and a multi-value Diameter field ('24, 30, 36'). Elsewhere in this same roster, GEM does NOT do this for structurally identical cases: the Sui-Multan corridor has FOUR separate PIDs -- P4090 (mainline) plus P4091/P4097/P4098 as 'Loopline I/II/III', each its own row with its own single diameter and length, even though they nominally parallel the same corridor. P4107 groups three non-continuous loop segments (different lengths, not sequential portions of one route) under one PID with a multi-diameter field, which is the pattern GEM normally reserves for a single continuous route whose pipe diameter changes along its length (e.g. P4019 Dadu-Malir-Karachi, dia='20, 18'), not for parallel/looped segments. Recommend either (a) splitting P4107 into three separate loopline rows analogous to Sui-Multan's I/II/III convention, each with its own single diameter and length, or (b) if kept as one row, add a ResearcherNotes entry documenting that the combined 129.95km/24,30,36-in fields represent three distinct SNGPL loop segments, not one continuous pipe of varying diameter -- so a future researcher doesn't misread it as the latter.

Extensive open-web search (Bing, attempted Google/DuckDuckGo -- both blocked by CAPTCHA/error pages) across many phrasings -- exact phrase "Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline", "Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline II", "Malakwal" + "SNGPL", "Malakwal" + "gas pipeline" + "Mandi Bahauddin", OGRA/SNGPL annexure searches for a transmission-line table -- returned ZERO results referencing this pipeline, any gas-transmission asset serving Malakwal town, or this name anywhere online. Every query either returned generic Faisalabad tourism/geography pages, SNGPL bill-payment portals, or entirely unrelated content (one query returned University of Guelph library pages). SNGPL's public transmission-system page (sngpl.com.pk/web/about-us/transmission-system/) 404'd, so the utility's own site did not yield a network map either. Web Archive (web.archive.org) is not reachable from this environment, so I could not check an archived snapshot of the gem.wiki page for citation leads.

Independently verified the two endpoints' coordinates via Wikipedia (a source unrelated to GEM, used only for geography, not cited as a pipeline source): Faisalabad 31.4167N 73.0911E; Malakwal (Mandi Bahauddin District, Punjab) 32.5531N 73.2067E. Straight-line (great-circle) distance between those points is ~126.6 km. This row's own LengthKnown value is 90.82 km -- LESS than the straight-line distance between its own stated StartLocation/EndLocation. A pipeline route can never be shorter than the straight-line distance between its endpoints, so this is a self-contained, verifiable data error independent of any external source: either the Length, or one/both endpoint names, is wrong, or this row is not really a Faisalabad-to-Malakwal line at all (e.g. a mislabeled sub-segment of a longer corridor). For comparison, sibling row P4128 'Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline' (no numeral) states 158.67 km, which comfortably clears the 126.6 km floor and is a physically plausible route.

Roster context: the wider 63-row roster contains several other same-corridor 'Pipeline' / 'Pipeline II' pairs with internally consistent-looking specs (P4106/P4107 Sidhnai-Faisalabad, P4135/P4136 Faisalabad-Shahdara I/II, P4161/P4162 Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah I/II, P4170/P4173 Wah-Nowshera I/II, P4108/P4140 Sahiwal-Lahore I/II), which argues the underlying table is probably a genuine SNGPL segment inventory rather than wholesale fabrication -- but that context does not rescue this specific row's internal length/endpoint contradiction, and I could not find one independent trace of THIS row anywhere to confirm it as a distinct, correctly-specified asset. Owner (SNGPL, 100%) is geographically plausible (SNGPL is the correct Punjab transmission operator) but likewise unconfirmed by any independent source.

No refs are proposed for Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Diameter, Location, or Owner on this row -- none could be independently verified, and per standing rules I will not fabricate a URL or force a citation onto an unverifiable value.

Found ZERO independent evidence that a 'Kot Momin-Jauharabad' gas pipeline exists. (1) Downloaded and visually inspected SNGPL's own official, current Transmission Network Map ('AS ON 30-06-2026', https://www.sngpl.com.pk/web/page.jsp?pgids=461 -> Transmission Network Map article -> https://www.sngpl.com.pk/web/images/transmission/TransmissionMap072026L.jpg, a 4800x7200 engineering drawing, Drawing No. T-1). Jauharabad DOES appear on the map, fed by an 8-inch line from Chashma (continuing on to Khushab/Shahpur) -- matching the diameter GEM records for P4133 and closely matching neighboring roster row P4134 'Jauharabad-Chashma Gas Pipeline' (82.21 km, 8in). 'Kot Momin' does NOT appear anywhere on this map -- not as a node, not as a line label -- including in the Bhera/Bhalwal Industrial Estate/Jhelum Crossing (Malakwal)/Sargodha corridor where Kot Momin geographically sits. (2) Checked geography: Wikipedia gives Kot Momin's coordinates as 32.18833N 73.02861E (Sargodha District, near Bhalwal, ~40km from Sargodha city, on the M2 motorway corridor) and Jauharabad's as 32.29194N 72.27361E (Khushab district HQ). These two towns are on OPPOSITE sides of Sargodha (Kot Momin to the east/southeast, Jauharabad to the west) -- there is no plausible direct transmission corridor between them on the current network, and none is drawn on SNGPL's own map. (3) The great-circle distance between the two named towns computes to ~72.0 km -- essentially identical to the GEM LengthKnown value of 72.41 km. That match (route length = straight-line town-to-town distance, not a measured pipeline route) is a classic bulk-load/geocoding artifact, exactly the failure mode flagged in this scope's orchestrator notes (implausible round/derived numbers from a single 2023-07-10 bulk load). By contrast, P4134's stated 82.21 km is close to (but sensibly longer than, i.e. plausible as an actual route atop) the ~79 km straight-line Chashma-Jauharabad distance -- P4134 looks real; P4133 does not. (4) Two independent web searches (via Bing, since WebSearch's session quota was exhausted) for 'Kot Momin' + 'Jauharabad' + gas pipeline, and 'Kot Momin' + gas pipeline + SNGPL, returned zero relevant results of any kind -- no news, no SNGPL/OGRA documentation, nothing. Conclusion: this row is very likely a fabricated/mis-parsed entity from the 2023-07 bulk load -- possibly a mangled duplicate split of the real Chashma-Jauharabad line (P4134) with a wrong start-point town substituted in, or a wholesale hallucination. PipelineType='transmission' and Owner='SNGPL' would both be plausible IF the line were real (SNGPL operates the whole Punjab network shown on this map, and 8in lines elsewhere in this bulk load are consistently classed transmission), so I am not raising separate classification/attribution flags -- the existence question is the threshold issue. Do NOT paste any of the below as a confirming reference for the current values; I have none to offer, deliberately.

However this is NOT a bare existence flag: this batch's own already-staged GulfPub (Petroleum Economist) reconciliation crosswalk (recon_gulfpub_crosswalk.json) independently corroborates that SNGPL operates a cluster of real, named 8-inch-diameter gas trunk lines in exactly this corridor -- Quaidabad-Chashma (44.573 km, composite 0.68, diam 8in, operator SNGPL), Chashma-Piplan (14.717 km, explicitly flagged 'PARTIAL COVERAGE -- corroborates this row's LOCATION only, not its length, capacity or extent'), Shakardara-Lachi (30.121 km) and two Lachi-Bakhar variants (140.2 km and 86.8 km) -- all attributed to SNGPL, all 8in diameter, matching GEM's Diameter=8in exactly and GEM's Owner1=SNGPL exactly. That is genuine independent (tier-2, single-source) evidence that SNGPL-operated 8in gas transmission infrastructure of this general type physically exists in the Khushab/Chashma corridor, so I am not calling this a phantom/hallucination. The problem is specific attribution: none of the independent GulfPub records use the name 'Jauharabad' -- the closest and best-scoring match is 'Quaidabad-Chashma' at 44.573 km (recon's own len_flag: 'DELTA 46%' vs GEM's 82.21 km). Wikipedia confirms Quaidabad is a separate town/tehsil in the SAME Khushab District as Jauharabad (the district's capital), on the same Lahore-Mianwali road that continues to Chashma -- so a real corridor Jauharabad->Quaidabad->Chashma is geographically plausible, and GEM's longer 82.21 km figure could legitimately be the combined Jauharabad-to-Chashma run (of which Quaidabad-Chashma is just the final ~45 km leg) rather than an error -- but that is a hypothesis, not something I could independently confirm this run. Separately: no duplicate risk found in the roster -- P4134 reads as the natural next segment after P4133 (Kot Momin-Jauharabad, 72.41 km, same 8in diameter, same LastUpdated batch), i.e. proper corridor segmentation (Kot Momin -> Jauharabad -> Chashma), not a double-count. Classification as 'transmission' is consistent with how SNGPL/GulfPub classify these long intercity 8in trunk lines (not gathering/distribution), so no classification concern. Net: existence of SOME real SNGPL 8in line to Chashma in this corridor is independently supported; the specific 82.21 km / 'Jauharabad' attribution on this exact row is not, and should be treated as unverified until someone with working search/gem.wiki access checks an SNGPL network map or OGRA report directly.

EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed by SNGPL's own 2006 Annual Report (sngpl.com.pk/download/AR2006/Page56-61.pdf), which has a dedicated section 'GAS SUPPLY TO MURREE' describing this exact project: 'The construction of Rawat-Murree line...The total length of 12" dia, Rawat-Murree transmission line is 58 Km while distribution supply mains were completed with a total length of 17 Km in first phase.' It states the line was commissioned in FY2005-06 and formally inaugurated by President Musharraf on 28 Aug 2006 -- the first gas pipeline built at that elevation (>6,000 ft) in Pakistan, crossing the Soan River. This is corroborated independently by Dawn: 'Effective plan to meet energy needs: Musharraf opens gas project' (dawn.com/news/146932) reporting the same Aug-2006 inauguration of a Rs600m Murree hills gas line, and by a later Dawn investigative piece (dawn.com/news/328997, 8 Nov 2008) 'Provision of gas to Murree rural areas still a dream', which independently confirms 'Gas supply project to Murree was inaugurated by...Pervez Musharraf in August 2006' while reporting that city consumers and rural settlements (Shawala, Sunny Bank, Kuldanna, Pindi Point, Cart Road, Jika Gali) still lacked service two years on -- i.e. the trunk transmission line was built and inaugurated on schedule, but downstream distribution build-out to end consumers in Murree town lagged for years afterward (a caveat about local distribution rollout, not about this transmission-line row's existence). Current-day operation is corroborated by a July 2026 news item (dailythedestination.com) reporting SNGPL busted an illegal 40m tap on 'SNGPL's main gas distribution line on Mall Road, Murree' at a hotel -- gas is demonstrably still flowing into Murree today, ~20 years after commissioning, matching Status=operating. CLASSIFICATION: SNGPL's own report calls it explicitly a 'transmission line' (as distinct from the 17km of 'distribution supply mains' built alongside it) -- GEM's PipelineType=transmission is correct and matches the primary source's own terminology. DUPLICATE: checked against the 63-row Pakistan-gas roster -- no other row touches Rawat or Murree; this is not a relabel/segment double-count of any other PID. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=SNGPL(100%) is confirmed both by the AR2006 (SNGPL's own report, 'the Company' undertook and commissioned it) and independently by the 2008 Dawn piece, which names 'The Sui Northern Gas Pipeline (SNGPL)' as the utility responsible for the Murree gas project. StartLocation/EndLocation (Rawat->Murree) are literally named by both the SNGPL report and the Dawn coverage. Rawat's province field (Islamabad) is defensible though administratively fuzzy -- open-web sources describe 'Rawat Fort' as a union council of the Islamabad Capital Territory, while a separate/overlapping 'Rawat' locality is also described as being in Rawalpindi District, Punjab; Murree's province (Punjab) is unambiguous. Not flagging this as an attribution error given the genuine dual designation. SPEC: Diameter=12in exactly matches SNGPL's '12" dia' figure -- direct match. LengthKnown=57.25km vs SNGPL's own rounded '58 Km' is a ~1.3% variance, well within normal rounding/as-built-survey tolerance -- not treated as a material spec disagreement. No independent numeric source was found giving a different (conflicting) length or diameter. Overall: this is a real, well-documented, correctly-classified SNGPL transmission line -- one of the very few genuinely notable/landmark pipelines in this bulk-loaded roster (unlike most of the other 62 rows, this one has substantial independent press coverage precisely because of its unusual high-altitude construction).

This is a real, bounded existence concern -- not 'this is almost certainly a phantom' but 'this specific row cannot be independently corroborated beyond GEM's own page, only the broader network it would belong to.'

The exact string 'Mian Channu-Hasilpur Gas Pipeline' / 'Mian Channun - Hasilpur' returns literally ONE public result anywhere on the open web: the gem.wiki page itself. No independent news article, company page, or report names this specific segment. This is consistent with it being one of dozens of short SNGPL sub-trunk segments in this bulk-loaded 2023-07 batch that simply have no individual English-language (or, as far as I could search, Urdu) public coverage -- SNGPL's own published PDFs (Exit Points Transmission Aug-2025 declaration-of-capacity table, 2006 transmission system map) list only large industrial/SMS exit points and do not mention Hasilpur, Mian Channu, or Khanewal by name, so absence there is not informative either way. Wikipedia's Hasilpur article does not mention gas infrastructure. OGRA's site returned 403. HOWEVER: I cross-checked this row against the country's own registered reconciliation dataset (GulfPub / Petroleum Economist PE World Map, batches/pakistan-gas/staging/recon-gulfpub-20260807/match_diff.json), which is an independent commercial geodatabase, NOT derived from GEM. It contains a record (ref_id gulfpub:gas:9688, 'Mian Channun - Hasilpur') that the reconciliation engine matched to P4174 with composite 0.868 / 'green' confidence: name similarity 0.98, diameter exact match (12in vs GEM's 12), length 0.99 similarity (GulfPub geodesic 84.986km / stated length 85.295km [=53 miles, correctly converted post the 2026-07-29 gulfpub-gas miles-fix] vs GEM's 83.85km, a 1.7% difference well within slack given GEM's own RouteAccuracy on this row is 'very low (straight line/schematic)'), owner exact match ('Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd' both sides), and status exact match (both 'operating'). GulfPub's own pipe_type field is 'National' (its transmission-tier bucket, not 'Distribution'), supporting GEM's PipelineType=transmission. NOTE ON GulfPub's OWN DATA QUALITY: comparing real-world coordinates, GulfPub's start point labeled 'Mian Channun' (72.566034, 29.695563) actually sits at Hasilpur's true location, and its end point labeled 'Hasilpur' (72.311084, 30.415219) sits at Mian Channu's true location -- i.e. GulfPub's own endpoint labels for this record appear transposed relative to real geography (the same swap recurs one record over: GulfPub's 'Hasilpur-Haroonabad' record, oid 9689, gives Haroonabad the coordinate that is actually Hasilpur's true location). This does not affect the length corroboration (distance A-B = distance B-A) and does not undermine that a real ~85km, 12in SNGPL transmission line connects the Mian Channu and Hasilpur corridor -- but it does mean I cannot lean on GulfPub's raw start/end labels as confirmation of *which* GEM StartLocation/EndLocation field is correct, only that the segment and its length/diameter/owner/status are real and match. I therefore treat this as MEDIUM-tier corroboration (one strong independent source, not directly public-URL-citable) rather than a full pass with a citable [ref]. CLASSIFICATION: no concern -- consistent with GulfPub's own tier and with every other roster row's uniform 'transmission' classification for this class of SNGPL town-to-town segment. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-row Pakistan-gas roster -- no other row names Mian Channu, Hasilpur, or this corridor; the GulfPub record nearest in spec ('CC1 - Lala Musa', oid 7153, same 12in/53mi values) is geographically unrelated (Gujranwala-area coordinates ~73.17-73.98E/32.57-32.71N vs this row's ~72.3-72.6E/29.7-30.4N) -- coincidental shared round numbers in the underlying network table, not the same pipe. Flagging a related but out-of-scope lead for Discovery/Update, not for this row: GulfPub also carries a 'Hasilpur - Haroonabad' record (oid 9689, 8in, ~64km) that the reconciliation engine could only place as AMBIGUOUS between P4133 and P4174 (neither a clean match) -- this looks like a further downstream continuation segment SNGPL operates past Hasilpur that may not have its own GEM ProjectID; worth a Discovery pass, not an edit to P4174. ATTRIBUTION: StartLocation Mian Channu (Khanewal District, Punjab) and EndLocation Hasilpur (Punjab) are both real, correctly-provinced places; no attribution concern. SPEC: Diameter (12in) and Length (83.85km) both corroborated as above within normal tolerance -- no material disagreement, so no spec concern raised. Net: real pipeline, correctly classified, not a duplicate, attributes plausible and independently corroborated by a non-GEM commercial dataset -- but because no public webpage could be found that names this specific segment (and GulfPub itself is not a citable public URL, and its own source_url field is just the generic https://www.sngpl.com.pk/ homepage which would fail url_verifier's value-presence check), I am NOT proposing any [ref] URL for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner on this row -- flagging as confirmed-with-caveat rather than a clean pass.
